channel.description: How to back up photos to a USB drive on Android — no cloud, no account, no upload.

item.title: How to back up photos to a USB drive without uploading them
item.description: Your photos don't need a cloud to be safe. A USB drive plugged into your phone holds the whole backup — no upload, no monthly fee, no account, and nobody else's server ever sees your pictures.

item.title: USB photo backup on Android: back up photos to an external drive without uploading them
item.description: Your phone's camera roll fits on a drive you can hold. A USB photo backup keeps the whole copy in your pocket — no upload, no monthly fee, no account, and nobody else's server ever sees your pictures.

item.title: How to back up DCIM to OTG storage on Android
item.description: DCIM is where your Android phone keeps its camera photos — and OTG is how a USB drive plugs straight into that phone. Put the two together and your whole camera roll copies to a drive you can hold, with no computer and no upload in between.

item.title: How to copy photos to a USB stick on Android
item.description: A USB stick is the simplest photo backup there is: no account, no upload, no monthly fee — just your photos on a drive you can hold. And on Android you don't need a computer in between: the stick plugs straight into the phone.

item.title: How to back up photos offline on Android — no cloud, no account
item.description: Most "backup" apps start by uploading your photos to someone else's server. An offline backup never does: your photos copy from your phone straight to a drive you can hold, with no account, no upload, and nothing to log into.

item.title: How to back up photos to an external drive on Android
item.description: An external drive is the simplest photo backup there is: a drive you can hold, with your photos on it, and no cloud in between. On Android the drive plugs straight into the phone — no computer needed.

item.title: How to free up space by moving photos to a USB drive
item.description: Your phone is full because your photos are. Move them to a USB drive you can hold, check the copy, then delete the originals — and the storage warning goes away without losing a single picture.
